title: Closing a switch on an uncharged capacitor
caption: Just after closing, V_C = 0, so the whole 10 V is across the 1 kΩ and I = 10 mA. As the capacitor charges, V_C = 10(1 − e^{−t/τ}) rises and the current I = 10e^{−t/τ} mA falls, with τ = RC = 1 ms. After a long time I = 0 and V_C = 10 V. At t = τ, V_C = 6.32 V and I = 3.68 mA.
alt: Graph with time in milliseconds: the capacitor voltage rising from 0 to 10 V and the current falling from 10 mA to 0, crossing at 5.00 at 0.69 ms.
description: The horizontal axis is time in milliseconds; the vertical axis shows V_C in volts and I in milliamperes on the same numbers.
Just after closing: V_C = 0, I = V/R = 10 mA.
The time constant is τ = RC = 1 ms; V_C = 10(1 − e^{−t/τ}) rises and I = 10e^{−t/τ} falls.
After a long time: I = 0 and V_C = 10 V.
